events.event_title: US-China Tariff Escalation & Trade War Resumption
events.event_description: The Trump administration has reimposed sweeping tariffs on Chinese goods, with rates on some categories exceeding 100%. China has retaliated with counter-tariffs and export controls on rare earth elements. This is actively reshuffling supply chains, pressuring importers, and creating winners among domestic manufacturers and alternative sourcing beneficiaries.
events.rationale: POWL (Powell Industries) benefits as US-made electrical equipment demand rises with reshoring. APOG (Apogee Enterprises) is a domestic glass/framing manufacturer insulated from Chinese competition. VRRM (Verra Mobility) has purely domestic revenue with no tariff exposure and benefits from infrastructure spending. CEVA (semiconductor IP licensor) faces headwinds as Chinese chip customers reduce licensing. BYRN (Byrna Technologies) is a small domestic manufacturer that could gain as buyers shift from Chinese-sourced alternatives.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $290 on volume >500k shares, or pullback to $280-282 support with RSI confirmation (>50). Confirmation of tariff implementation timeline and first supply chain reshoring announcements from major industrial customers.
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $278 (break of support), or tariff negotiations signal reversal/delay. Also exit if RSI falls below 40 on high volume, indicating institutional profit-taking before event clarity emerges.
tickers.risk: Tariff policy reversal or negotiated settlement reduces reshoring thesis; POWL's domestic margins may face wage/logistics inflation offsetting tariff benefits; mixed direction thesis limits conviction; execution risk on customer orders materializing; competition from other domestic manufacturers dilutes gains.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $37.50 on volume >500K shares with confirmation of tariff impact in construction/architectural glass sector; or pullback to $35.50 support on RSI <60 during tariff uncertainty headlines
tickers.exit_condition: Tariff negotiations show signs of resolution; OR RSI crosses below 50; OR price closes below $35.00; OR 6-week timeline expires without material upside
tickers.risk: APOG's domestic positioning thesis weakens if tariffs are rolled back; company has limited direct exposure vs. downstream beneficiary play; mixed timeframe creates event decay risk; RSI at 67.9 suggests limited room before overbought pullback

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $4.50 on volume >2M shares with confirmed RSI divergence from oversold extreme (13.9 RSI); or gap up on infrastructure contract announcement
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $4.15 (support break); tariff policy reversal/deal announcement; or time-stop at 6 weeks if thesis invalidated by earnings miss
tickers.risk: VRRM's domestic revenue insulation is already priced in; tariff escalation may depress overall economic growth and infrastructure spending; RSI extremes suggest potential dead-cat bounce; event conviction may shift rapidly on trade deal rumors

events.event_title: Rare Earth & Critical Minerals Export Controls by China
events.event_description: China has imposed export restrictions on rare earth elements including dysprosium, terbium, and other heavy rare earths critical for EV motors, defense systems, and semiconductors. The US has virtually no domestic processing capacity, creating acute near-term supply anxiety and a strong policy push for domestic alternatives.
events.rationale: MP Materials is the only US rare earth miner with active production and processing expansion underway — most direct beneficiary. UUUU (Energy Fuels) is expanding into rare earth processing from uranium sites. SGML (Sigma Lithium) benefits from broader critical minerals investment thesis. NMP (not to be confused) — focusing on UUUU and MP as primary plays. APLD is a stretch but data center operators are flagging supply chain risk in hardware dependent on rare earth magnets, drawing investor attention to domestic alternatives broadly.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $61.50 with volume >2M shares on geopolitical headlines OR pullback to $56-57 support with RSI <40 and fresh China export control news
tickers.exit_condition: Exit 50% at $68-70; trail stop at $54 for remainder. Close all positions if China reverses restrictions OR US announces major domestic processing capacity milestone reducing urgency
tickers.risk: Event-driven volatility can reverse quickly on diplomatic thaw; MP has execution risk on processing expansion; valuation already pricing some supply-shock premium; broader market correction reduces risk appetite for cyclicals

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $15.50 on volume >2M shares OR announcement of US government rare earth processing contract/funding for UUUU facilities
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $14.20 OR China reverses export restrictions OR competitor (MP Materials) significantly outperforms on quarterly guidance
tickers.risk: UUUU has lower processing capacity than MP Materials; execution risk on rare earth expansion timeline; policy reversal if US-China trade tensions ease; uranium segment volatility may overshadow rare earth tailwinds

tickers.entry_trigger: NMP closes above $10.50 on volume >2M shares with positive China export control headlines; or wait for pullback to $9.80-$10.00 on RSI <60
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >80 and close below 10-day MA, or 8% gain achieved, or geopolitical event reverses (China relaxes restrictions), or broader market correction >3%
tickers.risk: NMP is SPAC shell with no direct rare earth exposure—thesis applies to MP and UUUU, not NMP. Execution risk on domestic processing capacity timelines. China may moderate restrictions, deflating urgency. Event-driven trades compress quickly; timing is critical.

events.event_title: US Defense Spending Surge & NATO Burden-Sharing Push
events.event_description: The Pentagon budget proposal includes significant increases in missile defense, autonomous systems, and hypersonics. Simultaneously, European NATO allies are dramatically raising defense budgets under US pressure, creating export opportunities for US defense contractors — particularly second-tier specialists in munitions, drones, and electronic warfare.
events.rationale: RCAT (Red Cat Holdings) is a small-cap drone maker with direct DoD contracts for small UAS systems used in contested environments. KTOS (Kratos Defense) specializes in affordable drones and hypersonic target vehicles — exactly the systems being prioritized. AVAV (AeroVironment) makes tactical drones with strong NATO ally export pipeline. PLTR (Palantir) wins on AI-enabled battlefield software contracts accelerating under new defense priorities. HII (Huntington Ingalls) is the less-followed shipbuilder with nuclear submarine backlog that benefits from Pacific deterrence spending.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $13.50 on volume >2M shares OR confirmation of new DoD contract announcement within 2 weeks
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $11.80 OR profit target hit OR no contract news by week 8 of timeframe
tickers.risk: Small-cap liquidity risk; RCAT dependent on single/few contracts; DoD procurement delays common; competition from AVAV/KTOS with stronger balance sheets; geopolitical escalation priced in unpredictably

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $60.50 with volume >2M shares on Pentagon budget bill passage or NATO spending announcement; alternatively dip to $56-57 on profit-taking for re-entry
tickers.exit_condition: Take profits at $70+ on news catalyst; hard stop at $54.50 (below recent support); exit if competing contractor wins exclusive NATO drone contract or if defense budget proposal stalls in Congress
tickers.risk: Geopolitical de-escalation narrative, extended procurement timelines delaying revenue recognition, competition from Northrop/Lockheed capturing mid-tier contracts, supply chain delays, and valuation compression if broader defense sector underperforms

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $190 on volume >2M shares concurrent with Pentagon budget committee vote or NATO spending announcement; or pullback to $180-182 with RSI <55 during consolidation
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $178 (breaks recent support); or if Pentagon budget stalls in Congress beyond Q2; or take profits at $210 on 50% position; or hard stop if defense spending narrative reverses
tickers.risk: AVAV already priced in defense cycle optimism (stock +40% YTD typical for this thesis); export licenses face State Dept delays; European budget commitments remain aspirational without appropriations; competition from Northrop/General Atomics on larger NATO contracts; geopolitical de-escalation removes urgency

events.event_title: Commercial Real Estate Debt Maturity Wall & Regional Bank Stress
events.event_description: Over $950 billion in commercial real estate loans are maturing in 2025, with office vacancy rates still near historic highs. Regional banks holding concentrated CRE exposure face rising non-performing loans. The Fed's higher-for-longer rate posture is keeping refinancing costs punishing. Several mid-size banks are expected to report significant CRE charge-offs in coming quarters.
events.rationale: NYCB (New York Community Bancorp) has already disclosed CRE stress and remains vulnerable to further deterioration in NYC office/multifamily. OFG Bancorp has Puerto Rico CRE exposure that could be stressed. AROW (Arrow Financial) is a smaller community bank with concentrated regional CRE. COLB (Columbia Banking System) has elevated CRE-to-capital ratios post-merger. TBBK (The Bancorp) has niche exposure to commercial lending that warrants scrutiny. These are bearish swing candidates on any negative earnings guidance or credit quality disclosures.

tickers.entry_trigger: OFG closes below $45.00 on elevated volume (>2M shares) following negative CRE exposure disclosure or earnings guidance cut; or RSI drops below 50 on weakness
tickers.exit_condition: Take profit at $40.50 or below; stop loss if stock rallies above $47.50 on positive earnings surprise or Fed pivot signals; exit by week 8 regardless
tickers.risk: Puerto Rico economic recovery narratives could offset CRE concerns; Fed pivot to rate cuts would benefit regional banks; OFG's diversified revenue (insurance, wealth management) may cushion CRE deterioration; positive Q4 earnings surprise before maturity wall impact fully materializes

tickers.entry_trigger: Earnings miss with guidance cut on CRE provision expense or NPA ratio deterioration >25bps QoQ; alternatively, Fed stress test results showing capital ratio compression; RSI pullback below 55 on volume
tickers.exit_condition: Close above $39.50 or after 8 weeks if thesis hasn't materialized; stop-loss at $38.80 (technical support break + sentiment reversal)
tickers.risk: AROW's smaller scale may mean less CRE concentration than peers; regional deposit stability (upstate NY) may cushion losses; positive rate environment supports NII; crowded bearish positioning in regional banks could trigger short-covering rally
